text:
Terminal supervision is already part of original BERT4Rec: §3.6 explicitly adds training examples masking only the final item; inference appends [MASK] and reads its hidden representation. The paper describes this as fine-tuning-like, but the official README’s generator, gen_data_fin.py, mixes examples: D randomly masked copies plus one last-only-masked copy per sequence window, shuffled together. Thus explicit terminal-only examples constitute 1/(D+1), approximately 9.1% at default D=10; random masking can additionally select the terminal position. Simply adding terminal supervision is therefore established practice. [Paper](https://arxiv.org/html/1904.06690), [official generator](https://github.com/FeiSun/BERT4Rec/blob/master/gen_data_fin.py).

Random masking selects min(max_predictions_per_seq, max(1, round(length×ρ))) positions without replacement. Distinguish masked_lm_prob, which controls selection density, from mask_prob, which controls replacement: its default 1.0 means all selected items become [MASK], despite inherited comments mentioning 80/10/10. Official run.py computes full-vocabulary cross-entropy summed over valid targets, divided by their total count across the minibatch—not an equal-weight average of sequence losses. Consequently, terminal-example frequency and terminal gradient weight differ when random examples contain multiple targets. [Generator](https://github.com/FeiSun/BERT4Rec/blob/master/gen_data_fin.py), [loss implementation](https://github.com/FeiSun/BERT4Rec/blob/master/run.py).

Recommended controls: random-only masking; original mixed masking; terminal-only masking; proposed frequency/weighting with matched optimizer steps, target counts, and loss normalization. Separate frequency changes from explicit terminal-loss weighting and prefix sampling. Published ablations compare one random mask against multiple masks and sweep ρ; these do not isolate terminal-supervision frequency. Report any new benefit as a scheduling/weighting improvement within BERT4Rec, evaluated with the fixed RecHarness splits and validation protocol. [Paper, §§4.4–4.6](https://arxiv.org/html/1904.06690).
